record_reviews.summary: Lyell’s twenty-five surviving body blocks continue his 3 October critique of the Origin. He argues that creation could give Galápagos species a South American stamp, presses Lamarckian monad-production and progressive development, and says adding a principle of improvement makes selection indistinguishable from a mysterious creative power. He then comments on chapters X and XI, migration and specific centres, asks focused questions about primrose/cowslip intermediates, coccygeal vertebrae, rudimentary versus prophetic organs and Apteryx, and ends by predicting the book will mark an era. The body is not a catalogue synopsis: it contains Lyell’s direct objections and questions, with paragraph 13’s Gaudin/Heer report and blocks 14 and 16 acting as manuscript/page notes.
record_reviews.date_assessment: The TEI sent date is 4 October 1859 exactly (1859-10-04); the source note says the preserved text is mostly a contemporary copy in Mary Elizabeth Lyell’s hand, with an incomplete original scrap in DAR 170:81. Composition, copy/transmission, dispatch and Darwin’s receipt are separate; the body does not establish when Darwin received it.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Lyell is the incoming author of the surviving argument, but the physical witness is a copy and an incomplete autograph fragment. The Gaudin report, Heer report, Huxley quotation and references to Agassiz/Owen/Grove are embedded reported voices, while editorial footnotes supply later publication references and must not be treated as Lyell body prose.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 2501 is Lyell’s 3 October letter and supplies the opening proof-review exchange; 3132 is a distinct 4 October continuation. 2503’s wording about the long letter of 3d and still longer of 4th supports a two-input response, so the whole of 2503 cannot be assigned to either incoming letter alone.
2507 answers Lyell’s continuing climate/progression objections but does not identify these 4 October chapter questions as its sole prompt; it follows the exchange later in October.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The strongest candidate is the partial 3132→2503 reply. Lyell’s original 4 October letter is not fully preserved, and 3132 itself is mostly a contemporary copy with an incomplete autograph, so receipt and exact section-to-section attribution remain bounded.

record_reviews.summary: Lyell's 19-block letter says he has finished the Origin and praises its sustained reasoning, while recommending concrete examples in a future edition. He challenges Darwin on Lamarck and Geoffroy, the eye objection, condensed passages, Madeira birds and storms, and the relation of natural selection to a principle of improvement. He explicitly reports missing pages 400–409 and asks Darwin to send old proofs to Scarborough. This is a substantive incoming critique with multiple separable prompt spans; its direct preserved response is Darwin 2503, while later Pallas correspondence is a different exchange.
record_reviews.date_assessment: XML date is 3 October 1859 exactly; Lyell is the incoming author and Darwin the recipient. The letter records Lyell's completed reading, but not when Darwin received or answered it beyond Darwin's later acknowledgement. Paragraph 16 establishes missing proof pages as a documentary gap.
